breakfast.name: Kahwa wa Kleicha (Coffee and Cookies)
instructions: Mix dough with butter, sugar, cardamom, rose water
Fill with date paste or walnut-sugar
Shape into rounds or crescents
Bake at 175°C 20 min
Serve with Iraqi coffee
breakfast.description: Iraqi date-filled cookies — served at every celebration.

breakfast.name: Gaimer (Clotted Cream) with Bread
instructions: Spread thick gaimer on warm bread
Drizzle with date syrup
breakfast.description: Rich clotted cream on bread with date syrup — a classic Iraqi morning.

breakfast.name: Kahee (Iraqi Sweet Bread)
instructions: Make yeasted dough — let rise until doubled
Roll out thin, spread with melted butter/ghee
Fold and roll repeatedly — creating flaky layers (like puff pastry)
Roll out final time, cut into portions
Fry or bake until golden and puffed — the layers should separate
Sprinkle with sugar while hot
Serve with gaymar (Iraqi thick clotted cream) on top
The buttery layers with sugar and cream — rich, sweet, indulgent
This is Iraqi celebratory breakfast — Eid mornings and special occasions
breakfast.description: Iraqi celebratory breakfast bread — yeasted dough layered with butter, fried golden, dusted with sugar, and topped with gaymar (thick clotted cream). The flaky layers and the cream crown make kahee the most indulgent Iraqi morning treat, served every Eid.

breakfast.name: Timman wa Gaymar (Rice with Cream)
instructions: Cook rice until fluffy — Iraqi amber rice is the preferred variety
Serve hot rice in a bowl
Top with a generous spoonful of gaymar (thick clotted cream)
Sprinkle sugar and cardamom on top
Mix the cream into the hot rice — it melts into a rich, sweet porridge-like mixture
This is Iraqi breakfast simplicity — rice, cream, sugar
Gaymar is made by slowly heating milk and collecting the thick cream layer
The quality of the gaymar determines the quality of the breakfast
Simple but luxurious — carbs, fat, sweetness, comfort
breakfast.description: Iraq's simplest luxury breakfast — hot rice topped with gaymar (thick clotted cream), sugar, and cardamom. The cream melts into the rice creating a rich, sweet porridge. Gaymar is Iraq's contribution to the world's dairy traditions — thicker than clotted cream, richer than butter.

lunch.name: Quzi (Roast Lamb with Rice)
instructions: Roast lamb leg with baharat spices 2 hours
Cook saffron rice
Toast almonds and raisins in ghee
Serve rice mounded on platter topped with lamb
Scatter nuts and raisins
lunch.description: Iraq's celebratory lamb and rice — grand and aromatic.

lunch.name: Dolma (Stuffed Vegetables)
ingredients: Vine leaves, zucchini, eggplant, tomatoes, peppers
Filling: rice, ground lamb, tomato paste, parsley, dill, lemon
instructions: Hollow vegetables, blanch vine leaves
Mix filling
Stuff each vegetable tightly
Pack in pot, add water and lemon juice
Simmer 60 min
lunch.description: Assorted stuffed vegetables — a labor of love.

lunch.name: Tashreeb (Bread-and-Broth Stew)
instructions: Cook meat with onion, garlic, turmeric, baharat, dried lime — make a rich broth
Add chickpeas, simmer until everything is tender — 90 min for lamb
Tear flatbread into pieces, line the bottom of a deep dish
Ladle the hot broth and meat over the bread — the bread soaks it all up
The bread becomes soft and saturated, absorbing all the flavor
Add more broth — the bread should be swimming
Top with the meat and chickpeas
Tashreeb is Iraq's answer to French onion soup — bread soaking in broth
This is the most comforting Iraqi meal — broken bread absorbing lamb broth
Dried lime gives the uniquely Iraqi sour-bitter note
lunch.description: Iraq's bread-in-broth stew — flatbread torn and soaked in rich lamb broth with chickpeas and dried lime. The bread absorbs every drop of the fragrant broth. Tashreeb is Iraq's most comforting meal and the dried-lime sourness is the distinctive Iraqi flavor note.

lunch.name: Kubba Mosul (Stuffed Kibbeh from Mosul)
ingredients: Shell: bulgur wheat, semolina, ground meat
Filling: ground lamb, onion, pine nuts, raisins, baharat
instructions: Make shell: mix fine bulgur, semolina, and a bit of ground meat — knead until smooth
The shell dough must be pliable enough to shape but firm enough to hold
Make filling: sauté lamb with onion, pine nuts, raisins, baharat
Shape: take a ball of shell dough, hollow it out, fill with lamb mixture, seal
The shape should be torpedo-like or round — smooth with no cracks
Deep fry until dark golden — 5-6 min
The outer shell should be crispy-crunchy, the inside juicy and spiced
Mosul is famous for kubba — the city has dozens of kubba varieties
The pine-nut-and-raisin filling is the Mosuli signature — sweet-savory contrast
Kubba-making is an art — speed and smoothness of shaping shows skill
lunch.description: Mosul's famous stuffed kibbeh — crispy bulgur shells filled with spiced lamb, pine nuts, and raisins. Mosul is Iraq's kubba capital with dozens of varieties. The sweet-savory filling and the crispy-shell-then-juicy-interior bite make kubba Mosul one of Iraq's most skilled and celebrated dishes.

dinner.name: Masgouf (Grilled Carp)
instructions: Butterfly fish, rub with salt and tamarind
Stake fish near fire, skin-side to flames
Grill slowly 45 min
Lay skin-side down on coals to crisp
Serve with onion, tomato, lemon
dinner.description: Iraq's national dish — slow-grilled riverbank carp.

dinner.name: Tashreeb (Bread Soup)
instructions: Simmer lamb with chickpeas, tomatoes, spices
Tear bread into pieces in bowls
Ladle stew over bread
Squeeze lemon on top
dinner.description: Lamb stew poured over torn flatbread.

dinner.name: Masgouf (Grilled Carp — Iraq's National Fish)
instructions: Butterfly the carp — split open from the belly, spread flat
Rub with tamarind, turmeric, salt, olive oil
Stake the fish upright around a wood fire — the fish faces the flames
Grill slowly, indirectly, for 45-60 min — the smoke infuses the fish
The skin should be crispy, the flesh moist and smoky
When almost done, lay the fish flat over the coals briefly for the final char
Serve with tomato, onion, and Iraqi flatbread
Masgouf is traditionally prepared along the banks of the Tigris River in Baghdad
The riverside masgouf restaurants of Abu Nawas Street were legendary
This is Iraq's national fish dish — Mesopotamia's oldest culinary tradition
dinner.description: Iraq's national dish — whole carp butterflied and staked upright around a wood fire along the Tigris River banks. The slow-smoke-then-char technique is Mesopotamian and ancient. The riverside grilling scene and the 'world's oldest culinary tradition' claim make masgouf Iraq's most storied dish.

dinner.name: Biryani Iraqiyya (Iraqi Biryani)
instructions: Brown meat with onion, baharat, dried lime, tomato paste
Add water, simmer until meat is tender
Parboil rice with whole spices — drain at 70% done
Layer in pot: meat on bottom, rice on top, fried onion, saffron milk, almonds, raisins
Seal and cook on very low heat — 30-40 min
The Iraqi biryani is simpler than the Hyderabadi version but the baharat gives it a distinct flavor
The dried lime (loomi) is what makes it Iraqi — the sour-bitter note
The tahdig (crispy bottom) is valued here too
Serve on a large platter, inverted so the meat is on top
dinner.description: Iraqi biryani — the Mesopotamian take on the great rice dish, distinguished by baharat spice blend and dried lime (loomi). Simpler than the Indian version but with a distinctive sour-bitter note from the dried lime that no other biryani tradition uses.

dinner.name: Dolma (Iraqi Stuffed Vegetables)
ingredients: Grape leaves, zucchini, eggplant, onion, tomato, pepper (all for stuffing)
Filling: rice, ground lamb, tomato paste, dill, parsley
instructions: Prepare vegetables: hollow out zucchini, eggplant, onion, tomato, pepper
Blanch grape leaves briefly
Make filling: mix rice, ground lamb, herbs, tomato paste, spices
Stuff each vegetable — pack tightly but leave room for rice expansion
Roll grape leaves around filling — tight cylinders
Layer stuffed vegetables in a large pot — tight, so they don't unravel
Add tomato sauce, dried lime, water — the sauce cooks the rice
Cover, simmer 90 min until rice is cooked and vegetables are tender
The variety of stuffed vegetables is the Iraqi distinction — 7+ types in one pot
Iraqi dolma uses more types of vegetables than any other Middle Eastern version
dinner.description: Iraq's legendary dolma — seven or more types of vegetables (grape leaves, zucchini, eggplant, onion, tomato, pepper) stuffed with herbed rice and lamb. Iraqi dolma uses more vegetable types than any other Middle Eastern version, making the multi-colored pot reveal one of the most photogenic moments in Iraqi cooking.

snacks.name: Samoon (Iraqi Flatbread)
instructions: Mix dough, rise 1 hour
Shape into diamond loaves
Press sesame seeds on top
Bake at 230°C 10 min

snacks.name: Samoon (Iraqi Diamond Bread)
instructions: Make yeasted dough — let rise until doubled
Shape into diamond or football shapes — the traditional Iraqi bread shape
Slash the top, sprinkle with sesame seeds
Bake at high heat until golden and puffed — 12-15 min
The bread should be light, airy inside, with a golden crust
The diamond shape is iconic — every Iraqi recognizes samoon
This is Iraq's everyday bread — from bakeries (furns) all over Baghdad
The sesame seeds on top are the signature
Fresh samoon from a brick oven is one of life's simple perfections
snacks.description: Iraq's everyday diamond-shaped bread — golden, sesame-topped, and puffed from a brick oven. Every Iraqi neighborhood has a furn (bakery) producing samoon from dawn. The distinctive diamond shape and the sesame crust are Iraqi bread identity.

snacks.name: Kleicha (Iraqi Date Cookies)
ingredients: Dough: flour, butter, yeast, cardamom, rose water, mahlab
Filling: dates (pressed into paste with cinnamon, cardamom)
Or filling: walnuts with sugar and cardamom
instructions: Make enriched dough with butter, cardamom, rose water, mahlab (cherry kernel spice)
Rest dough 30 min
Make date filling: press dates into a smooth paste with cinnamon and cardamom
Roll out dough, spread date paste, roll into a log, slice into rounds
Or: shape as half-moons with walnut filling
Brush with egg, sprinkle sesame seeds
Bake at 175°C for 15-20 min until golden
Kleicha are Iraq's national cookie — served at Eid, weddings, every celebration
The date version is more traditional; the walnut version is equally beloved
Every Iraqi family has a kleicha recipe — and a kleicha mold
snacks.description: Iraq's national cookie — date paste (or walnuts) wrapped in rose-water-and-cardamom dough, shaped with traditional molds. Kleicha are at every Eid, every wedding, every Iraqi celebration. The date-cardamom flavor and the ornate mold patterns make kleicha one of the Middle East's most beloved cookies.

desserts.name: Zalabia (Fried Pastry in Syrup)
instructions: Mix thin batter, let rise
Make rose water syrup
Pipe batter in circles into hot oil
Fry until crispy
Soak in syrup
desserts.description: Crispy fried spirals soaked in rose water syrup.

desserts.name: Znoud el Sit (Lady's Arms Pastry)
ingredients: Cream filling: ashta/gaymar (clotted cream) or thick custard
Sugar syrup: sugar, water, rose water, lemon juice
instructions: Make sugar syrup: boil sugar and water, add rose water and lemon — keep warm
Make cream filling: thick ashta (clotted cream) or semolina custard
Cut phyllo into rectangles, place cream filling at one end
Roll into cigar shapes — tight, neat cylinders
Fry until golden and crispy — 3-4 min
Immediately dip in rose-water sugar syrup — they soak it up
Garnish with crushed pistachios
The outside is crispy-syrupy, the inside is cool cream — temperature and texture contrast
The name 'Lady's Arms' refers to the shape — plump, rounded cylinders
These are Ramadan favorites — served at iftar across Iraq
desserts.description: Iraq's cream-filled cigar pastries — crispy fried phyllo cylinders filled with clotted cream, soaked in rose-water syrup, and garnished with pistachios. The crispy-hot-exterior-meets-cool-cream-interior contrast makes znoud el sit a Ramadan favorite and one of the most satisfying Middle Eastern pastries.

desserts.name: Baklava (Iraqi Style)
instructions: Layer phyllo sheets in a pan, brushing each with melted butter
Every 3-4 sheets, sprinkle a layer of ground walnut-pistachio-cardamom mix
Continue layering until all phyllo and nuts are used — 20+ layers
Cut into diamond shapes before baking — must be cut before, not after
Bake at 175°C for 25-30 min until deeply golden and crispy
Pour COLD rose water syrup over HOT baklava — the temperature difference ensures crispiness
Let soak for hours — overnight is best
Iraqi baklava uses more cardamom than Turkish — the flavor is distinctive
The walnut-pistachio mix rather than pure pistachio is the Iraqi style
Baklava-making is a social event — families gather to assemble
desserts.description: Iraqi baklava — layers of phyllo and walnut-pistachio mix with heavy cardamom, soaked in rose-water syrup. Iraqi baklava distinguishes itself with its generous cardamom and the walnut-pistachio blend. The cold-syrup-on-hot-pastry technique for maximum crispiness is the baker's secret.

desserts.name: Halawat al Jibn (Sweet Cheese Rolls)
instructions: Heat cheese until it melts and becomes stretchy
Add semolina to the melted cheese — stir until combined into a dough
Flatten the cheese-semolina dough on a surface — spread thin
Cut into rectangles, place cream filling along one edge
Roll into cylinders — the warm cheese dough wraps around the cool cream
Drizzle with sugar syrup
Garnish with crushed pistachios
The warm stretchy cheese with cold cream inside — the temperature contrast is magical
This is Iraqi-Syrian sweet tradition at its best — sweet cheese is a concept
The cheese dough being stretchy and sweet shocks first-timers
desserts.description: Iraqi sweet cheese rolls — stretchy melted cheese mixed with semolina, rolled around cold clotted cream, and drizzled with rose syrup. The 'sweet CHEESE?!' concept shocks first-timers, but the stretchy-warm-cheese-meets-cool-cream sensation converts them instantly.

drinks.name: Iraqi Chai (Cardamom Tea)
instructions: Boil water with cardamom
Add tea, steep 5 min
Sweeten well
Serve in istikan glasses
drinks.description: Strong, sweet tea with cardamom — drunk all day in Iraq.

drinks.name: Arak
instructions: Distill grape spirit with aniseed
Triple distill for clarity
Mix with water and ice to serve (turns milky white)
drinks.description: Anise-flavored spirit — turns cloudy with water.

drinks.name: Chai Iraqiyya (Iraqi Tea)
ingredients: Black tea (strong — Iraqi tea is DARK)
instructions: Boil water in a large kettle
In a smaller teapot, add generous tea and cardamom pods
Pour boiling water over, let steep until very strong and very dark
The tea should be almost opaque — much darker than English or Iranian tea
Pour into small istikan glasses — the tulip shape is iconic
Add sugar — generous, Iraqis like their tea sweet
The cardamom floats in the glass — part of the charm
Tea is served constantly in Iraq — morning, noon, night, with every guest
Refusing tea in an Iraqi home is almost impossible — hospitality demands it
The istikan glass shape is the visual signature of Iraqi tea
drinks.description: Iraqi tea — jet-black, sweet, cardamom-scented, served in tulip-shaped istikan glasses. Iraqi tea is darker and sweeter than any other Middle Eastern tea tradition. The iconic glass shape and the 'refusing tea is impossible' hospitality culture make Iraqi chai a viral cultural symbol.

drinks.name: Sharbat (Iraqi Fruit Syrup Drink)
ingredients: Rose water or fruit syrup (lemon, orange blossom, tamarind)
instructions: Make or buy concentrated fruit/flower syrup
Dilute with cold water to taste
Add ice
Add chia seeds if desired — they swell and create a unique texture
The rose water version is the most traditional
Serve ice cold — sharbat is summer survival in Iraq's 50°C heat
The word 'sherbet' in English comes from 'sharbat' — Arabic origin
This is Iraq's oldest cold drink tradition — centuries old
The chia seed addition (they swell into gel-coated seeds) is uniquely Iraqi
Pink rose sharbat in a glass is one of the prettiest drinks in the world
drinks.description: Iraq's ancient cold drink — fruit or flower syrups diluted with iced water, sometimes with chia seeds that swell into gel-coated pearls. The English word 'sherbet' comes from Arabic 'sharbat.' Pink rose sharbat in a glass is one of the world's most beautiful drinks.

drinks.name: Noomi Basra (Dried Lime Tea)
ingredients: Dried limes (loomi/noomi basra — black or yellow)
instructions: Pierce dried limes with a knife or crack them open
Add to boiling water — steep like tea for 10 min
The water turns a golden-amber color
The flavor is sour, slightly bitter, citrusy, earthy — complex
Add sugar if desired — many Iraqis drink it unsweetened
Dried lime tea is Iraq's caffeine-free alternative to regular tea
Noomi Basra means 'lime of Basra' — Iraq's port city in the south
The dried lime is Iraq's most distinctive spice — used in cooking and as a drink
The flavor profile is unlike any other tea or tisane in the world
Health benefits: digestive, rich in vitamin C
drinks.description: Iraq's dried lime tea — the uniquely Iraqi spice brewed into a golden-amber, sour-earthy tisane. Named after Basra, Iraq's southern port city. The flavor is unlike any other tea in the world. The dried-lime-as-beverage concept and the Basra origin story are fascinating culinary geography.
